families.name: Tests with Coverage
families.guidance: The ordinary PR path fixes four groups in both the workflow matrix and scripts/run_pr_test_shard.py (including its argument choices and pytest --splits value). Change those coupled entry points together if the reviewed plan changes the shard count; use the existing duration-based complete selection rather than dropping tests. Inspect pr-test-diagnostics artifacts because the test-command step can contain a timeout-only second attempt. Preserve the stable Tests with Coverage aggregate and its lint/shard failure propagation. Extend tests/test_pr_test_duration_weights.py or a focused orchestration regression, and run bash scripts/test.sh with only the affected test files.

families.name: Complete source tests
families.guidance: Source CI already creates immutable complete plans with a 420-second estimated-work target and a 12-shard cap. Inspect the source-duration and source-test-plan artifacts before increasing parallelism: queue/setup/aggregation can dominate workflow latency even when every shard is short. Preserve exact selected inventory, plan digest, same-attempt receipts, and the Complete source tests with Chromium aggregate. Reuse the planner and current native duration history rather than introducing another splitter. Verify with bash scripts/test.sh tests/test_source_ci_orchestration.py tests/test_ci_shard_plan.py; measure actual job/step timings separately from native pytest phase estimates.

families.name: Browser Tests
families.guidance: Separate Chromium download/apt/preflight costs from the browser-marked pytest step. Keep all browser-marked tests, real browser preflight, and hard failure when required Chromium cannot launch. A partition must preserve browser marker selection and native failures. Use bash scripts/test.sh with the affected browser orchestration/regression selection; do not turn browser prerequisites into skips.

families.name: OpenCode Live Tests
families.guidance: Distinguish pinned CLI installation and runtime image preparation from the live-test step, which already runs pytest with two workers. Preserve all opencode_live-marked tests and exact checked-out runtime image preparation. Additional shards duplicate image setup and may be slower; inspect the job steps and existing diagnostics before choosing partitions. Run the affected live regressions through bash scripts/test.sh with required Docker/OpenCode prerequisites available.

families.name: Muse Live Tests
families.guidance: Inspect pinned real-host installation separately from muse_live conformance execution. Keep the pinned executable checksum and all real-host cases; do not replace native assertions with mocked success to reduce time. Run bash scripts/test.sh tests/test_muse_background_live.py -m muse_live with its declared real-host prerequisite.

families.name: Worker processes and bridge
families.test_step_pattern: ^Test real worker processes and management bridge$
families.guidance: The retained worker-bridge job runs separate worker-bridge and worker-daemon invocations and emits native result/timing artifacts. If splitting these invocations, preserve both complete explicit test lists, invocation identities, result receipts, and the Supervisor Integration Tests aggregate. Keep real-process cleanup and failure propagation; do not substitute helper-only tests. Verify selected real-process cases with bash scripts/test.sh and inspect resulting artifacts.

families.name: Python 3.14 compatibility
families.job_pattern: Python 3\.14 (?:non-live tests \(\d+/\d+\)|source quality and (?:non-live tests \(advisory\)|complete test plan))
families.guidance: This advisory workflow checks Python 3.14 using locked dependencies and a complete non-live test selection. Keep the interpreter/lock assertions, real Chromium preflight, and complete not-opencode_live selection. Inspect setup and collection costs before choosing balanced test partitions; preserve advisory status rather than making unrelated merge gates stricter. Run affected lock/workflow regressions through bash scripts/test.sh tests/test_ci_uv_lock_policy.py.
